name: Arkansas
summary: Statutes: the official Arkansas Code is a LexisNexis JavaScript app (link-only); quote from Justia's 2025 edition (tier 2, WebFetch, one subtitle hop), and read session-law PDFs from arkleg.state.ar.us by constructible URL. Constitution: Justia per-section pages; the SOS PDF is on an unconfirmed ark.org host. Court rules and opinions live on opinions.arcourts.gov (Lexum): the script reads opinions via item/{id}/index.do?iframe=true but gets 403 on document.do, so court-rule text needs the fetch tool. Public-domain citations (2024 Ark. 181) since 2009; review denials are in Supreme Court proceedings lists found by docket search. Admin rules: the official Code of Arkansas Rules (2025-) is script-readable by NEXT-walking; the legacy SOS rules search is robots-blocked.

citation_map.notes: No law_aliases: Ark. Code Ann. cites are title-chapter-section; the Justia URL needs a subtitle that is not in the citation (one index hop). 'Ark. Code Ann.', 'A.C.A.', 'Ark. R.', 'Ark. Sup. Ct. R.', 'Ark. Const.' and 'N CAR §' are Arkansas markers; a bare '§ 16-56-105' routes here only with 'of the Arkansas Code'. Ranges ('§§ 16-56-101 to -130') capture only the first section. Arkansas constitution articles are cited with Arabic numerals (art. 2, § 13); amendments are numbered (amend. 80). Public-domain citations 'YYYY Ark. N' / 'YYYY Ark. App. N' (opinions from July 1, 2009, per Ark. Sup. Ct. R. 5-2 from memory) cannot collide with Ark. Reports volumes (official reports ended at about 375 Ark. / 104 Ark. App. in 2009). Court of Appeals rules are in the joint 'Rules of the Supreme Court and Court of Appeals' (Rule N-N). Bare 'Rule 5-2', 'Rule 37.1 petition', dockets 'CR-20-170' and S.W. cites are context_required. Unreported/older unpublished CoA opinions are cited by docket and date; from 2009 every opinion carries a neutral cite. Rules pattern accepts 'Ark. R. Prof. Conduct' and the undashed 'Ark. R. App. P. Civ.' (independent check 2026-10-17).

access.pattern_rules: title, chapter, section from the citation, unpadded. subtitle is NOT in the citation: open the title page (lists 'Subtitle N - name', no chapter ranges) or the subtitle page (lists chapter links, no section ranges) to find the subtitle holding the chapter. subchapter = the section's hundreds digit in the usual case (16-56-105 → subchapter-1; 16-56-201 → subchapter-2); do not rely on the chapter page for section ranges: one WebFetch summary showed them (chapter 56) and another did not (chapter 88). Default to the hundreds digit and confirm on the section page itself (NOT PRESENT or 404 → try the chapter page's other subchapter links). Undated path = current edition; /codes/arkansas/2024/… for older editions.
access.navigation: title page (subtitle names only, no chapter ranges; may take several subtitle-page fetches to find the chapter) → subtitle page (chapter links) → build subchapter-{hundreds digit}/section-{t}-{c}-{s}/ and confirm the body on the section page. Verified: § 16-56-105 → /title-16/subtitle-5/chapter-56/subchapter-1/section-16-56-105/; § 5-10-102 → /title-5/subtitle-2/chapter-10/subchapter-1/section-5-10-102/; § 4-88-107 → /title-4/subtitle-7/chapter-88/subchapter-1/section-4-88-107/.

sources.coverage: Each rule set is one document: Civil Procedure (item 16712), Evidence (1876), Appellate Procedure–Civil (1885), Appellate Procedure–Criminal (1884), Rules of the Supreme Court and Court of Appeals (1871), Criminal Procedure (1879), Professional Conduct current (1868), District Court Rules (1878), Code of Judicial Conduct (1874), Amendments-Adoptions-Updates (18217), and others.

access.pattern_rules: item = rule-set id from the listing (16712 Civ. P., 1876 Evid., 1885 App. P.–Civ., 1884 App. P.–Crim., 1871 Sup. Ct. & Ct. App. Rules, 1879 Crim. P., 1868 Prof. Conduct). The whole rule set is one page; find the rule inside it.
access.navigation: listing (iframe=true form returns the list to the script) → item/{item}/index.do?iframe=true shows 'Rule Current To' date only → text at {item}/1/document.do (fetch tool). When a rule set's text is needed: (1) WebSearch for 'opinions.arcourts.gov/ark/cr/en/{item}/1/document.do' and WebFetch the URL as returned by the search (this worked for 1876); (2) if no search result carries it, treat the rule as link-only: cite and link {item}/1/document.do, do not quote. Corpus extraction of the rule sets is the lasting fix.

sources.title: Arkansas Judiciary opinions (Supreme Court and Court of Appeals, Lexum)
sources.publisher: Arkansas Supreme Court / Reporter of Decisions
sources.official_status_evidence: Item pages carry a 'Neutral Citation' field (2024 Ark. 181; 2021 Ark. App. 21); from July 2009 the court's own web opinions are the official report under Ark. Sup. Ct. R. 5-2 (from memory, rule text not fetched).
sources.coverage: Supreme Court from 1837 (1837 date listing has 13 items), Court of Appeals from 1979 (reported); scanned Ark. Reports for older cases (e.g. 304 Ark. 32 with S.W.2d parallel).

access.pattern_rules: court = supremecourt | courtofappeals. id is an internal item number. Find it by (a) date listing https://opinions.arcourts.gov/ark/supremecourt/en/{year}/nav_date.do?iframe=true, or (b) full-text GET search https://opinions.arcourts.gov/ark/en/d/s/index.do?cont={terms}&iframe=true — a quoted docket number (cont=%22CR-20-170%22) returns the opinion plus the proceedings lists that mention it. Searches containing 'Ark.' (citation strings) and the ref= parameter returned 403.
access.navigation: search/listing → item/{id}/index.do?iframe=true (metadata: Date, Neutral Citation, Docket Number, Author, then full opinion text with slip page numbers) — the script reads this; {id}/1/document.do is the same text for the fetch tool. Listing links lack ?iframe=true: append it before reading. If a docket search 403s, fall back to the year date listing (supremecourt/en/{year}/nav_date.do?iframe=true).

automation.robots_txt: Disallow for * only 4 specific item/document URLs; BUbiNG disallowed /
automation.notes: Script 403 (refused) on document.do, the host root, courtofappeals nav_date listings, and searches containing 'Ark.'; item/{id}/index.do?iframe=true and supremecourt listings return 200. Without iframe=true item pages are only menus. WebFetch reads document.do from search-result URLs; built item URLs were gated. Search engines often index the proceedings ('syllabus') lists instead of opinions. Alternate-path check (2026-10-17, maintainer): the publisher's own year listings link each opinion as item/{id}/index.do and {id}/1/document.do; robots.txt permits item pages, so reading the item page is the publisher's linked case page, not a workaround. The 403s on document.do and other URLs are per-URL refusals and are never retried.
